title: Scaling to Long Horizons — Ross Taylor & Chengxi Taylor, General Reasoning
talk_summary: A research talk from General Reasoning about scaling RL training to long-horizon agent tasks, covering compaction, value models, pipeline RL, and environment infrastructure.

takeaways.what_they_do: When the context window fills, the agent summarizes and continues on top of the summary; they also give the agent file-system tools as an external scratchpad for reasoning notes, plus self-search over prior trajectory and archive tools for building on earlier results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: generate the token until the end of the context window, summarize, and then on top of that generate more tokens

takeaways.technique: Bootstrap partial-trajectory signal instead of waiting for completion
takeaways.what_they_do: For very long episodes they use a value model to estimate expected outcome before the episode ends, so training/compute isn't idle waiting for a weeks-long run to finish; they explicitly note this trades GPU utilization against value-model bias.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before the end of the episode, you generate expectation ... that allows you to train the model
takeaways.numbers: off-policy up to eight steps is okay

takeaways.technique: Long-horizon benchmark with real-world open-ended task
takeaways.what_they_do: They built KellyBench, letting agents build ML models to trade football matches over a one-year horizon, arguing current benchmarks over-index on narrow coding/procedure tasks and under-test open-ended, multi-player, uncertain environments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the AI industry is a little bit too biased towards coding and procedure task
takeaways.numbers: all frontier models given 100K lost money

takeaways.technique: Hosted environment platform behind one API
takeaways.what_they_do: They run 350+ environments behind a single API endpoint for internal RL and external labs, treating environment infrastructure as a first-class concern for long-horizon work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: host over 350 environments and with a single API endpoint
